newsitem.title: USA: US spot heat loses intraday luster, jet tumbles.
newsitem.headline: US spot heat loses intraday luster, jet tumbles.

text.p: U.S. spot heating oil prices ended sharply lower Thursday after careening from five-year highs reached earlier in the day, players said, with New York jet fuel tumbling almost three cents a gallon amid oversupply and heavy selling.

Jet fuel prices caused a big stir, as traders watched diffs on New York Harbor 54-grade plunge a full two cents to about 0.25 cent below the print, dragging Gulf Coast material 0.75-cent lower to 1.30 cents below the screen.

"Citgo was dumping lots of barrels. They were taking any deals they could get," one East Coast jet trader said. "They've probably been sitting on a bunch of it for a long time and wanted to take some profits."
But a Citgo spokesman downplayed the day's events, saying, "From what I understand, we haven't done anything out of the ordinary."
NYMEX heating oil for October delivery had risen to a post-Gulf War high in the morning of 72.80 cents but reversed direction to settle at 70.90 cents -- almost 0.90 cent lower than Wednesday.
